note: Track minor-colours, mix step 4: natural, harmonic and melodic minor told apart by their 6th and 7th. One staff with a Variant selector over the three scales (no copy of the tool per scale), harmonic against melodic over the A minor chord, then lines that climb in melodic minor and fall in natural minor in a second key, with a line that says what stays. No moves, since the variant section names its selector. Missing: a listening tool that plays two scales one after the other for any instrument (the guitar-play-along's two-scales stands in, listened to only), and no game plays a minor scale to name.

exercise.title: Natural, harmonic or melodic minor
exercise.why: The three minor scales share their first five notes and differ only in the 6th and the 7th, so the top of the scale tells you which one you are hearing.

cells.text:
The staff below shows a minor scale on A, with its 6th and 7th ringed. Tap from {{5}} up to the {{1}} above it, through the two ringed notes.
Once you can hum the two ringed notes before you tap them, try the other two minor scales. Use the Variant selector below to change the scale.
When you change the scale, the notes up to {{5}} stay and only the ringed notes move: {{b6}} and {{b7}} in natural minor, {{b6}} and {{7}} in harmonic minor, {{6}} and {{7}} in melodic minor.

Press Play below to start the backing track: the A minor chord for eight bars, four in A harmonic minor, then four in A melodic minor. Follow the notes view and listen for the bar where one note changes: {{b6}} goes up a half step to {{6}}.
Practice until you can say "harmonic" or "melodic" without looking at the notes.

Press Play below to start the drone on D. On the first staff under it, D melodic minor, tap up from {{5}} through the ringed {{6}} and {{7}} to {{1}}. Then on the second staff, D natural minor, tap down from {{1}} through the ringed {{b7}} and {{b6}} to {{5}}.
Now make up lines of your own that climb on one staff and fall on the other.
Practice until you can tell a line's scale from its top notes alone.
On D the notes are new, and the three scales still differ only in the 6th and the 7th.
